title: Cluster E (Taganrog family) — P5989 likely double-counts P7817+P7818 as a completed corridor; P1457's 516 km is unconfirmed; P1488 is unrelated

rows.recommendation: Recommend to Update: reconcile P5989 (Taganrog-Melitopol, 272.73 km, operating since 2024) against P7817+P7818, which record the same Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk restoration at stale 'construction'/'proposed' statuses. The arithmetic and the reported build narrative line up too closely to be coincidence: P7817 (104.50 km) + P7818 (68.93 km) = 173.43 km for the restored Soviet trunk Taganrog->Mariupol->Berdyansk; P5989 minus that = 272.73 - 173.43 = 99.30 km, matching the independently reported 'more than 100 km' new Berdyansk-Melitopol extension (Kommersant, RIA Novosti). Kommersant's 2022-07-13 piece (kommersant.ru/doc/5459063, verified) describes the Russian Ministry of Energy's plan as explicitly TWO parts: (1) restore the existing but disused Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk trunk, (2) build a genuinely new >100 km Berdyansk-Melitopol section. That is exactly the geography P7817 (Taganrog-Mariupol, under reconstruction) + P7818 (Mariupol-Berdyansk, proposed extension) individually cover, and exactly the through-route P5989 now shows as completed and operating. No source anywhere in this search — including gem.wiki's own outbound citations, read only to harvest leads (2025 DNR Minstroy planning order confirming Taganrog-Mariupol 'underway' / Mariupol-Berdyansk 'proposed') — describes a SEPARATE, independently justified Taganrog-Melitopol asset distinct from the restored trunk plus its extension. Recommend Update fold P7817+P7818's status forward to match P5989 (i.e. treat them as superseded/merged into the now-operating P5989 corridor) or, if segment-level tracking is wanted, update P7817/P7818 statuses to 'operating' to match P5989 rather than carrying three simultaneous statuses (construction + proposed + operating) for one physical corridor. CONFIDENCE CAP: every source found is Russian state media or the DNR/Zaporizhzhia occupation administration (Kommersant, RIA Novosti, ura.news, which itself syndicates Kommersant) — one government announcement reprinted by aligned outlets is ONE origin per the corroboration rule; no Ukrainian government, ISW, or Western trade-press confirmation was found despite searching. Tier medium, not high, on the duplicate finding itself, though the arithmetic match is what makes it more than speculation.
rows.notes: P5989's own two citations name only Taganrog and Melitopol (per the task brief) — neither names Mariupol nor Berdyansk, so the overlap is not provable from P5989's citations alone; it is established here by cross-referencing the independently reported build narrative and length arithmetic. Sources checked and verified live: kommersant.ru/doc/5459063 (2022-07-13, 'Российский газ дотянется до Запорожья' — states the >100 km Berdyansk-Melitopol figure and the two-part restore+extend plan, and that the old corridor 'was partially unused since the 2009 gas conflict' i.e. needs partial not full rebuild); ria.ru/20220719/gazoprovod-1803530880.html (2022-07-19 — Zaporizhzhia occupation head Yevgeny Balitsky announces the Berdyansk-Melitopol build, no length given); ria.ru/20221025/gaz-1826622360.html (2022-10-25 — gas reaches Berdyansk first, per occupation figure Vladimir Rogov, with Melitopol to follow); neftegaz.ru's follow-up (2022-10-31, gas begins flowing to Melitopol households) corroborates the completion date range but the page is JS-rendered and its live text could not be extracted for a substring check — cite with that caveat if used. All of the above ultimately trace to ONE Russian government decision (Deputy PM Khusnullin's July 2022 directive) reported through aligned state/occupation channels — this is single-origin, medium tier by the standing rule, not two independent origins. Owner/attribution flag: P5989 carries a blank Owner while 'operating'. No source names a specific legal operator for the restored/extended line — occupation-administration statements attribute oversight to Russia's Ministry of Energy (Minenergo) as the sponsoring federal body, not a named pipeline operator, and Gazprom is documented (neftegaz 2014 reporting) as the historical owner of the original 1950s Taganrog-Mariupol trunk only, before its 2009 closure — that attribution does not automatically carry to a post-2022 occupation-built asset. GEM should NOT default Owner to either the Gas TSO of Ukraine (which does not operate in occupied territory) or Gazprom (unsourced for this specific restored/extended asset) — leave Owner blank and document the ambiguity in ResearcherNotes rather than guessing.

rows.recommendation: Companion row to P5989 above — same recommendation: reconcile status against P5989's 'operating since 2024' rather than leaving this segment at 'construction'. A 2025 DNR Ministry of Construction planning order (cited on gem.wiki as an outbound reference only, not itself cited here — I could not independently retrieve the primary document at minstroy-dpr.gosuslugi.ru despite searching) reportedly still describes the Taganrog-Mariupol segment as underway as of 2025, which would be internally consistent with 'construction' — but is now in tension with 2022 press describing gas already reaching Berdyansk/Melitopol downstream of this very segment. That tension itself is the reconciliation question for Update: either the segment was substantially complete enough to pass gas by late 2022 while formal capital-works documentation continued into 2025, or the 2022 gas-delivery reporting and this row's 'construction' status cannot both be describing the same completed asset without a status update.
rows.notes: 104.50 km merged length, 700 mm, Taganrog->Mariupol. No independent primary source located that states this exact 104.50 km figure — the only figure found for the historical Taganrog-Mariupol segment specifically is 33 km at Du 1020 mm (mytaganrog.com, verified live; corroborated by search-snippet-only sourcing not independently fetched). 700 mm also does not match the 1020 mm/1000 mm figures reported elsewhere for the old trunk, consistent with this row representing a NEW, differently-sized replacement pipe laid in the same corridor rather than the original Soviet pipe — which would explain why length figures diverge from the 33 km historical figure (a wholly reconstructed line does not have to match the old pipe's routing exactly). This is plausible but unconfirmed; flagging as a spec question for Update rather than asserting it.

rows.recommendation: Same companion recommendation as P7817: reconcile 'proposed' status against P5989's 'operating since 2024', which already reports this Mariupol-Berdyansk geography as complete and flowing gas since October 2022 per RIA Novosti reporting. If P7818 is being carried at 'proposed' because of the DNR Minstroy 2025 planning-document status gem.wiki cites, flag that document's date/scope explicitly in ResearcherNotes when Update touches this row, since it postdates 2022 reporting of gas already flowing past this segment.
rows.notes: 68.93 km merged, 500 mm, Mariupol->Berdyansk. No independent source located for the specific 68.93 km/500 mm figures. Ura.news (syndicating Kommersant) and RIA both report the road-distance framing that Mariupol-Berdyansk was part of the pre-existing (if disused) Soviet corridor, not new pipe — consistent with reconstruction of an existing route rather than a from-scratch build, which fits a 'proposed'-to-'construction'-to-eventually-'operating' lifecycle that may simply be stale here relative to P5989.

rows.recommendation: Flag P1457's 516.00 km 'merged' length for Update to re-verify. Every source located for the original Soviet-era Taganrog-Mariupol trunk gives ~33 km at Du 1020 mm (mytaganrog.com, verified; corroborated by search-snippet material referencing capacity of ~350,000 m3/hour to south Donetsk-oblast industry before the 2009 closure) — nothing found supports a 516 km figure for a Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk line, and the road distance Taganrog->Berdyansk along the Azov coast is itself only on the order of 150-200 km, well short of 516 km. Do not assume 516 km is wrong outright (I could not find where GEM's figure originates, and 'merged' network length can legitimately exceed corridor route distance if it aggregates multiple parallel strings or a longer upstream feed into Taganrog that this search did not surface) — but this is exactly the kind of length claim Update should chase to its origin rather than leave standing unchallenged, given how sharply it diverges from every other length figure found for this corridor.
rows.notes: P1457 = 'retired' 2009, matching every source's closure date for the original trunk. Its relationship to the reconstruction (P7817/P7818/P5989) is straightforward and not itself a duplicate concern: it is the correctly-retired predecessor whose right-of-way the restoration reuses, per Kommersant's own framing ('the old pipe... was partially unused since the 2009 gas conflict' — i.e. the same physical trench, not a new corridor). The open question is narrowly the 516 km figure, which this search could not source.

rows.recommendation: No action needed for this cluster. P1488 (Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol, 185.73 km, 1000 mm, operating since 1999) is a distinct inland corridor approaching Mariupol from the north/Donetsk direction, not the coastal Taganrog-Berdyansk corridor this cluster concerns. Nothing in this research suggests any overlap with P1457/P7817/P7818/P5989.
rows.notes: Included in the cluster roster per the task brief's framing (both feed Mariupol) but no source or structural signature ties it to the Taganrog restoration project. Recorded here only so the next sweep does not re-raise it as an open question in this cluster.

sources.what: Kommersant, 2022-07-13, 'Российский газ дотянется до Запорожья' — the pivot source: names the two-part plan (restore disused Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk trunk + build new >100 km Berdyansk-Melitopol section), states the old corridor needs partial not full reconstruction, gives the >100 km figure for the new section, no diameters given.
RIA Novosti, 2022-07-19 — Zaporizhzhia occupation administration head Yevgeny Balitsky announces the Berdyansk-Melitopol pipeline build via Telegram; timeline claims, no length/diameter.

sources.what: RIA Novosti, 2022-10-25 — gas reaches Berdyansk first (per occupation figure Vladimir Rogov), Melitopol named as next; confirms the Taganrog-Melitopol corridor's completion window.
URA.news syndication of the Kommersant report — same >100 km figure, same two-part plan, adds that neither Gazprom nor Minenergo commented for the record.

sources.what: Local Taganrog news portal tag page — confirms the original Taganrog-Mariupol trunk built in the 1950s and closed in 2009; used only for the closure-date/build-decade corroboration and the 33 km/1020 mm figures found in accompanying search snippets (page itself is a tag/index page, not the underlying article).

summary:
Cluster E's live question — does P5989 (Taganrog-Melitopol, 272.73 km, operating since 2024) double-count the same physical corridor that P7817 (Taganrog-Mariupol, 104.50 km, construction) + P7818 (Mariupol-Berdyansk, 68.93 km, proposed) already record — resolves toward a confirmed but medium-confidence, single-origin duplicate. Kommersant's 2022-07-13 report describes the Russian Ministry of Energy's plan in exactly two parts: restore the existing (if disused since 2009) Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk trunk, and separately build a genuinely new Berdyansk-Melitopol extension reported at 'more than 100 km'. P7817+P7818 sum to 173.43 km for the restored-trunk portion; subtracting that from P5989's 272.73 km leaves 99.30 km — matching the independently reported new-extension length closely enough (within normal rounding of a press estimate) that this reads as the same underlying project recorded twice: once as two stalled/in-progress segment rows, once as a single completed through-route. RIA Novosti's October 2022 reporting that gas reached Berdyansk then Melitopol supports P5989's 'operating' status and simultaneously undercuts P7817/P7818 still sitting at 'construction'/'proposed' — one physical corridor cannot honestly be construction, proposed, and operating all at once, which is itself the strongest evidence something needs folding or a status update.

The honest caveat, held to the same standard as a refutation would be: every source for this narrative is Russian state media or the occupation administration itself (Kommersant, its RIA and ura.news echoes, and the Zaporizhzhia/DNR officials they quote) — one government project announcement reprinted by aligned outlets is ONE origin by the standing corroboration rule, not two independent confirmations. No Ukrainian government statement, ISW report, or Western energy trade-press coverage of this specific pipeline surfaced despite dedicated searching. So the duplicate finding is reported at medium confidence, not high, and Update should treat the fold/status-reconciliation as the right move without treating the numbers as beyond challenge.

P1457 (the retired 516 km original) is the correctly-retired predecessor whose right-of-way is being reused, but its 516 km figure is unconfirmed by any source found — every source instead gives ~33 km/1020 mm for the historical Taganrog-Mariupol segment specifically, a sharp enough divergence to flag for Update without asserting it is wrong outright. P1488 (Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol) is a distinct inland corridor with no sourced or structural tie to this cluster.
open_questions: Should P7817 and P7818 be folded into P5989, or updated in place to 'operating' to match it — and if folded, does P5989 need to be split back into segments for RouteAccuracy/route-creation purposes?
What is the correct legal/operational Owner for P5989 in occupied territory? No source names one; do not default to Gazprom or the Gas TSO of Ukraine without further sourcing.
Where does GEM's 516 km figure for P1457 originate, given every source found gives ~33 km for the historical Taganrog-Mariupol segment specifically?

Does the 2025 DNR Minstroy planning document (cited on gem.wiki, not independently retrieved here despite searching minstroy-dpr.gosuslugi.ru) actually describe P7817/P7818's geography, or a different capital-repair phase overlapping the same route?
